why_angle: The cited rivals compare installed batteries by their spec sheets and installed prices. None reports a measured idle draw or measured energy delivered for any candidate. So none shows that a plug-in battery idling at 58 W loses about 31% of its delivered energy a day, while one idling at 10 W loses about 5%. That gap decides how long it lasts in a multi-day outage.
unsourced: OUPES Mega 1 idle draw with the inverter on: I looked in The Solar Lab's review, Bob Vila's review (Mark Wolfe), CleanTechnica's test (Jennifer Sensiba), the OUPES manual on ManualsLib, and OUPES's standby-consumption support article. That article lists only the Mega 2, 3 and 5. The table cell gives the manual's 6-hour no-load auto-off instead.

EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X measured energy delivered: The Solar Lab's review gives idle draw only, so the row uses EcoFlow's rated capacity. us.ecoflow.com returned HTTP 429 to storecheck today, so the $7,899 price is the angle agents' storecheck reading from 2026-11-15.
EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra: The Solar Lab gives about 82% efficiency without saying what load it used, so the Wh delivered is arithmetic.
Anker SOLIX S5000 240 V output under load: Andrew Riha (pv magazine) did not test it. The 4,500 W L14-30R figure is Anker's rating.
Tesla Powerwall 3 standby draw from a lab or a named reviewer: only owner logs on Tesla Motors Club were available, and the cell says so.

page.title: Best Home Battery Backup System: Plug-In Batteries Compared by Idle Drain
page.h1: Best home battery backup system for power outages
page.desc: Home battery backup systems compared on energy delivered in reviewers' tests, idle draw with the inverter on and 240 V output, plus where a wired Tesla Powerwall 3 fits.
page.answer: Short answer. The best home battery backup system you plug in is the Anker SOLIX S5000: about 10 W measured idle draw costs it 5% of its 4.87 kWh a day, against 31% for the 58 W Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus. For wired whole-home backup, Tesla Powerwall 3 (13.5 kWh, 11.5 kW) is the pick.

page.after:
What the differences mean

Dealectric does not test units. Every figure on this page is either a named reviewer's measurement or the maker's rating. The derived figures below are our arithmetic.

Idle loss per day = idle draw × 24 h ÷ energy delivered. Days to drain = energy delivered ÷ that daily loss, with the inverter on and nothing plugged in.

  • Anker SOLIX S5000: 10 W × 24 h = 240 Wh; 240 ÷ 4,870 = 4.9% a day; 4,870 ÷ 240 = about 20 days.
  • EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X: 36 W × 24 h = 864 Wh; 864 ÷ 12,288 Wh rated = 7.0% a day; about 14 days.
  • BLUETTI Apex 300: 19.5 W × 24 h = 468 Wh; 468 ÷ 2,290 = 20% a day; about 4.9 days.
  • EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra: 3,072 Wh × 0.82 = 2,519 Wh delivered; 22 W × 24 h = 528 Wh; 528 ÷ 2,519 = 21% a day; about 4.8 days.
  • Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus: 58 W × 24 h = 1,392 Wh; 1,392 ÷ 4,450 = 31% a day; about 3.2 days. On HOBOTECH's figure of 2,060 Wh a day, it is 46%, about 2.2 days.
  • OUPES Mega 1: 1,779 W × 27 ÷ 60 h = 800 Wh delivered at a heavy load.
  • Tesla Powerwall 3: 1.5 to 2.64 kWh a day (110 W × 24 h = 2.64 kWh) ÷ 13.5 kWh = 11–20% a day, from owner logs.

Cost per kWh for the two context rows: DELTA Pro Ultra X, $7,899 ÷ 12.288 kWh = $643/kWh before a transfer panel. Powerwall 3, about $15,000 installed ÷ 13.5 kWh = about $1,110/kWh.

Your needFitsWhy
Multi-day outage on small loads: fridge, router, CPAPAnker SOLIX S5000About 10 W idle. Ran a large fridge, phones and small devices for 61.5 h, from 100% to 18%, in a real utility shutoff (Riha)
240 V well pump, dryer or AC circuit through a transfer switchJackery Explorer 5000 PlusHeld 7,200 W at 240 V for 5 min (HOBOTECH). Switch the inverter off between uses
Heavy 120 V appliances, fast refill from the wall or a generatorEcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra3,600 W; 0–100% in 2 h on a household outlet (The Solar Lab)
Start small at 120/240 V and add batteries laterBLUETTI Apex 30019.5 W idle; stacks to 3 units and 18 batteries (ESS News)
One 2,000 W appliance on a small budgetOUPES Mega 1Ran 1,779 W for 27 min (The Solar Lab)
Whole house wired in, with solarTesla Powerwall 311.5 kW continuous, 13.5 kWh, 10-year warranty (Tesla)

Why idle draw decides a long outage

A plug-in battery's inverter uses power whenever it is switched on, even when nothing is plugged in. In a two-hour outage that hardly matters. In a three-day outage, with a fridge cycling on and off, the inverter's own draw can be one of the biggest loads in the house. Andrew Riha (pv magazine) left the S5000's 120 V output on with nothing connected, and it lost 5% in 24 hours, close to Anker's 8.8 W claim. The Solar Lab measured 58 W on the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus. HOBOTECH logged 515 Wh in 6 hours on the same model, which it put at 85 W. Tristan Rayner (ESS News) watched an Apex 300 draw about 19.5 W with its inverters on, in line with BLUETTI's 20 W figure. The Solar Lab measured about 36 W on the DELTA Pro Ultra X and about 22 W on the DELTA 3 Ultra.

On a wired system, the efficiency figure to use is Tesla's 89% round trip for Powerwall 3 (25°C, beginning of life, 3.3 kW). The 97.5% figure Tesla also publishes is solar-to-home efficiency, which skips the battery.

The fix costs nothing: switch the AC inverter off when nothing needs it. The OUPES Mega 1 does this itself after 6 hours with no load, and you can change that timer in the app.

Weak points to know before buying

  • Anker SOLIX S5000 {buy:anker-solix-s5000}: Anker's page says orders placed from November 6 ship in 9–10 weeks. It weighs 97 lb. Riha found it wobbly and prone to tipping on grass, and it has no 12 V DC output. He did not test its 240 V output. Anker gives a 5-year warranty.
  • Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus {buy:jackery-explorer-5000-plus}: it held 7,200 W at 240 V in HOBOTECH's test, but The Solar Lab found it struggled to start a 10,000 W-surge air conditioner. It weighs 134 lb (The Solar Lab).
  • EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra {buy:ecoflow-delta-3-ultra}: 120 V only. The Solar Lab connected a 1,000 W solar array to its 800 W input and the unit smoked, twice. It weighs 72 lb.
  • OUPES Mega 1 {buy:oupes-mega-1}: 120 V only. The Solar Lab found its voltage sagged on surge loads and called its fans 'very, very loud', a problem indoors during a blackout.
  • BLUETTI Apex 300 {buy:bluetti-apex-300}: Outdoor Life measured 83% of its rated capacity delivered (2,290 of 2,765 Wh), so size one unit for about 2.3 kWh of real use.
